rules.cwe_name: Data Processing Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
rules.description: Building a database query from user-controlled sources is vulnerable to insertion of malicious code by the user.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Building a shell command string with values from the enclosing environment may cause subtle bugs or vulnerabilities.

rules.cwe_name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
rules.description: Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

rules.cwe_name: Expression is Always True
rules.description: An equality comparison between two values that cannot be meaningfully converted to the same type will always yield 'false', and an inequality comparison will always yield 'true'.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
rules.description: A string transformer that does not replace or escape all occurrences of a meta-character may be ineffective.

rules.cwe_name: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
rules.description: Placing sensitive data in a GET request increases the risk of the data being exposed to an attacker.

rules.cwe_name: Numeric Truncation Error
rules.description: The integer shift operators '<<', '>>' and '>>>' only take the five least significant bits of their right operand into account. Thus, it is not possible to shift an integer by more than 31 bits.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.
